method_a.name: Method A — Strict Issue Proxy
method_a.description: Same customer, same product/SKU, same category within 30 days of resolution.
method_a.limitations: Category is an issue proxy, not ground truth, because agents may re-tag tickets upon closure.

potentially_avoidable_scenarios.note: Not all repeat contacts are avoidable. Avoidable savings require triage checklists and repeat alerts.

method_b.name: Method B — Product Proxy
method_b.description: Same customer, same SKU within 30 days of resolution.
method_b.limitations: Product-level repeat proxy, NOT exact same-issue detection. Captures cross-category escalation journeys.

potentially_avoidable_scenarios.note: Not all repeat contacts are avoidable. Avoidable savings require triage checklists and repeat alerts.

method_c.name: Method C — Text-Supported Issue Matching
method_c.description: Same customer, within 30 days, same SKU, and token overlap Jaccard >= 0.15.
method_c.limitations: Deterministic text similarity. Fails when customers write brief procedural follow-ups rather than re-explaining symptoms.

potentially_avoidable_scenarios.note: Not all repeat contacts are avoidable. Avoidable savings require triage checklists and repeat alerts.

method_d.name: Method D — Customer-Level Baseline
method_d.description: Same customer contacts again within 30 days across any product or category.
method_d.limitations: Upper bound of customer re-contact volume; includes unrelated subsequent inquiries.

potentially_avoidable_scenarios.note: Not all repeat contacts are avoidable. Avoidable savings require triage checklists and repeat alerts.

colleague_hypothesis_evaluation.hypothesis_text: Customers contacting repeatedly saying 'I already told your colleague this'
colleague_hypothesis_evaluation.conclusion: Hypothesis supported in substance: while the literal phrase 'told your colleague' does not appear, 115 messages contain explicit protests about previous unresolved contacts. Method A detects 81.74% and Method B detects 85.22% of these cases.

candidate_business_problems.title: Repeat Support Contacts & First-Contact Resolution (FCR) Breakdown
candidate_business_problems.observed_volume: 3,270 tickets (Product Proxy: Method B) / 1,412 tickets (Strict Issue Proxy: Method A)
candidate_business_problems.observed_rate: 27.54% (Method B) / 11.89% (Method A) of all support tickets
candidate_business_problems.cost_type: Observed handling cost calculated using Support Policy §4 channel interaction rates
candidate_business_problems.trend: Upwards (+155.8% volume increase between H1 2025 and H1 2026 concurrent with overall ticket growth)
candidate_business_problems.concentration: Returns Desk (35.5% repeat rate under Method B), Charging & Battery (32.6%), Pulse 2 earbuds (966 repeats under Method B)
candidate_business_problems.controllability_by_support: High. Frontline diagnostic checklists, repeat alerts, and handover notes fall directly under support desk operations.
candidate_business_problems.evidence_quality: High. Deterministic timestamp sequence tracking within 30-day window per Support Policy §10; validated by 115 explicit repeat complaint messages.
candidate_business_problems.limitations: Lack of explicit issue_id in database requires proxy definitions. Not all repeat contacts are avoidable.
candidate_business_problems.operational_hypotheses: Hypothesis: premature closure and inconsistent handover notes may contribute to repeat contacts; the available ticket data does not establish causality.
candidate_business_problems.actionability: Deploy automated repeat-contact banner alerts at intake and mandate diagnostic completion checklists before ticket resolution.

candidate_business_problems.title: Hardware Defect Outflows & Complaint Concentration in Flagship Products (Pulse 2 & Nexa 2)
candidate_business_problems.observed_rate: 39.19% of all support tickets; 86.14 complaints per 100 orders on Pulse 2, 94.28 per 100 orders on Nexa 2
candidate_business_problems.eighteen_month_cost: Rs 3,868,220.00 combined (Refunds: Rs 2,921,050.00 across 878 tickets; Replacements: Rs 947,170.00 across 457 units)
candidate_business_problems.cost_type: Observed refunds from accounting records; replacement inventory unit cost plus policy logistics benchmark (Rs 340/unit)
candidate_business_problems.trend: Upwards (+153% to +172% in hardware defect categories: Charging & Battery, Audio Quality, Connectivity)
candidate_business_problems.concentration: Pulse 2 True Wireless Earbuds (Rs 2.17M outflow) and Nexa 2 Smartwatch (Rs 1.70M outflow). Represents 48.74% of all refund dollars.
candidate_business_problems.controllability_by_support: Low to indirect. Support operations cannot fix manufacturing or firmware defects directly, but controls symptom telemetry and return qualification.
candidate_business_problems.evidence_quality: High. Deterministic join between orders.csv and tickets.csv; verified accounting refund sums and replacement flags.
candidate_business_problems.limitations: Detailed supplier manufacturing batch codes and return inspection logs are not in the dataset.
candidate_business_problems.operational_hypotheses: Hypothesis: hardware lot defects and Bluetooth companion app instability drive high complaint rates; factory QA logs are needed to verify root cause.
candidate_business_problems.actionability: Provide structured defect telemetry to hardware engineering and implement interactive frontline pairing/charging triage to reduce false returns.

candidate_business_problems.title: First-Response SLA Breaches & Store Credit Liabilities
candidate_business_problems.cost_type: Exact policy-mandated liability: Rs 350 store credit per breach under Support Policy §3
candidate_business_problems.trend: Stable breach rate across quarters (7.8% to 11.2%), with highest breach rates in May-June 2026
candidate_business_problems.concentration: Email Frontline has highest breach rate (11.56%, 440 breaches, Rs 154,000 credit liability)
candidate_business_problems.controllability_by_support: High. Workforce shift scheduling, agent staffing, and queue routing are within support desk operational control.
candidate_business_problems.evidence_quality: High. Exact timestamp differences between created_at and first_response_at compared to policy targets.
candidate_business_problems.limitations: Measures only initial response; does not capture full resolution time or customer response delays.
candidate_business_problems.operational_hypotheses: Hypothesis: staffing imbalances across shifts and weekend queues may contribute to first-response breaches; schedule logs are needed to verify causality.
candidate_business_problems.actionability: Rebalance agent shifts between Bengaluru and Indore; deploy automated 15-minute queue expiration alerts.

candidate_business_problems.title: Internal Team Routing Friction & Transfer Re-handling Benchmark Cost
candidate_business_problems.cost_type: Benchmarked re-handling cost: Rs 305 per transfer based on Support Policy §4
candidate_business_problems.trend: Concentrated in helpdesk period (transfers were not recorded in legacy_fd system)
candidate_business_problems.concentration: Chat Frontline (377 transfers) and Email Frontline (235 transfers) transferring to Escalations & Warranty and Logistics
candidate_business_problems.controllability_by_support: Moderate. Intake classification tags and automated routing rules can reduce misrouting.
candidate_business_problems.evidence_quality: Moderate to High. Direct integer count from helpdesk transfers field; cost is benchmarked rather than direct ledger outflow.
candidate_business_problems.limitations: Does not prove all transfers were unnecessary; transfers to Tier 2 are structurally required for warranty evaluations.
candidate_business_problems.operational_hypotheses: Hypothesis: customer misclassification at intake may increase transfer frequency; routing audit required to determine reducible share.
candidate_business_problems.actionability: Deploy intake triage classifier to route warranty claims and shipping issues directly to specialist queues on first touch.

candidate_business_problems.title: Payment Gateway Debit Failures & Billing Refund Drain (DUP-PAYMENT)
candidate_business_problems.observed_rate: 4.47% of all tickets (25.23% of all refund tickets)
candidate_business_problems.cost_type: Directly observed refund payouts from accounting records
candidate_business_problems.trend: Consistent throughout 18 months, mirroring e-commerce transaction volume peaks
candidate_business_problems.concentration: Billing Support team handles 100% of these cases; tickets typically have High or Urgent priority
candidate_business_problems.controllability_by_support: Low for support desk (requires payment gateway engineering and webhook reconciliation); high for customer communication.
candidate_business_problems.evidence_quality: High. Explicit refund reason code DUP-PAYMENT with exact refund amounts.
candidate_business_problems.limitations: Payment gateway server logs are not in the support ticket dataset.
candidate_business_problems.operational_hypotheses: Hypothesis: webhook dropped events during payment gateway authorization lead to customer accounts being debited without order creation.
candidate_business_problems.actionability: Escalate to payment gateway engineering for automated server-to-server transaction reconciliation.
